subject: Proposal: Dedicated GPU slice for nightly batch simulations (pilot)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Chris Tan <chris.tan@vertexbio.com>
Cc: procurement@vertexbio.com
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Dedicated GPU slice for nightly batch simulations (pilot)

Hi team,

VertexBio has confirmed they want to run their pilot workload on Redwood Dedicated. The ask: a nightly batch simulation window (heavy token generation + long sequences) that runs for ~4 hours overnight for their model family (vb-sim-7B). They expect three parallel jobs each night, peak ~750 concurrent streams for short bursts during checkpointing.

Attached is a rough allocation_proposal_v2.xlsx with estimated vGPU hours and a draft nightly_sweep_runbook.md. Key asks:
- Temporary dedicated carve-out: 1 x 8-GPU pool (can be fractional if needed), 0200-0600 local PT, Monday–Friday, for an initial 6-week pilot
- Autoscaling policy exception: allow the pool to burst beyond standard per-tenant caps during the 0200-0600 window by up to 2x for 10–15 minute bursts
- Preemption/eviction SLA: Vertex needs a 30-minute heads-up if eviction is imminent (we may need a webhook or paging integration)

Questions for infra/ops: what routing or isolation constraints do we need to protect other Dedicated customers? For product: what telemetry/validation do we require during the pilot to sign off on expansion?

Chris — we looped infra (Dev) and capacity (Hannah) to surface tradeoffs. If procurement needs a timeline, let me know the latest signoff date; Vertex is targeting Sept 5 start.

Next steps I propose:
1) Dev/Hannah: feasibility + rough timeline by EOD Aug 23
2) Marcus: provisional approval path for a temporary carve-out (conditions)
3) Marissa/Vertex: finalize SOW and procurement link

Thanks,

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Strategist, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

Attachments: allocation_proposal_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), nightly_sweep_runbook.md (markdown)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Dedicated GPU slice for nightly batch simulations (pilot)

Thanks Marissa — quick clarifying questions from infra so we can size this correctly:

- When you say "3 parallel jobs" — are those independent Kubernetes jobs each spinning up an entire model replica, or are they streams multiplexed onto a smaller number of replicas?
- What is the expected average seq length and the long-tail seq length? (affects memory and kv-cache sizing)
- Is low-latency (<100ms) required for check-point bursts, or is throughput the only concern?

From a mechanism perspective we can:
- Provision a temporary dedicated GPU pool (8 GPUs) pinned to a tenant in the Dedicated control plane
- Configure an autoscale override for the 0200-0600 window with a burst budget; need product signoff on the policy UI change or we can use an operator-only flag for the pilot

If Vertex is okay with a short canary night (single job on night 1) we can do a staged rollout and measure token-per-hour and preemption behavior.

I’ll review the attached allocation_proposal_v2.xlsx and post notes.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Infrastructure Lead, Serving Runtime
dev.patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Proposal: Dedicated GPU slice for nightly batch simulations (pilot)

Adding preliminary capacity perspective.

Quick notes after a first pass on allocation_proposal_v2.xlsx:
- 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs for 0200–0600 M-F looks reasonable for initial nights, total expected run-hours ~160/week
- Conflict risk: we have an existing pilot carve-out in the same region with a recurring weekly job (internal ML QA) that currently uses 2 GPUs in that window; we can shift them by an hour to create breathing room, but ops needs a defined window change request
- Autoscale exception: we can allow a 2x burst for 15 minutes every hour if we mark this pool as "pilot-exempt" in the reservations system. That will require a short runbook change (I attached a draft link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleLinkAllocation)

Operational caveats / requirements:
- We need a preemption notification mechanism (webhook) — ops can emit an event to Vertex’s webhook endpoint; legal needs to sign off on data in logs if Vertex asks for request-level traces
- Logging: retention for this pilot should be at least 30 days for postmortem; if Vertex wants full request logs longer than 30 days we will need a data-retention amendment

I recommend a staged ramp: two canary nights (single job), then three nights at 50% capacity, then full overnight run. That should surface model-specific memory pressure before full carve-out.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Capacity & Allocations Manager
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few items from Vertex procurement and engineering: 

- Procurement timeline: we need a signed SOW and PO by Sept 1 to hit the Sept 5 pilot start. If Redwood can offer a provisional carve-out with an internal approval doc, we can accept a subsequent formal SOW for billing.
- Heads-up requirement: 30-minute preemption notice is fine; we can accept a webhook-based notification and will integrate it into our job scheduler.
- Data retention: Vertex can accept 30-day request-level logs for the pilot. If longer retention is needed we’ll handle that via a separate agreement.

Engineering note: we will run a single canary job night-0 as proposed, then ramp to 50% on night-2. We don’t require sub-100ms latencies for this workload; throughput and stability are the main concerns.

If Redwood can provide a provisional carve-out approval document for procurement, that will unblock us.

—Chris
Chris Tan
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, VertexBio

Provisional approval granted with the following caveats (please make these explicit in the carve-out doc):
1) Autoscale cap: allow 2x bursts during 0200–0600 but set a hard upper-bound consumption threshold for the tenant to prevent noisy-neighbor impact; infra to implement a rate-limiter fallback if bursts exceed the budget for more than 30 minutes across the window.
2) Preemption notice: ops must emit a webhook and page Vertex engineering if an eviction is planned in <30 minutes.
3) Telemetry & logging: 30-day retention for request-level traces; longer retention subject to legal/data amendment.
4) Billing: provisional internal memo OK, formal SOW and PO required by Sept 5 for continued runs beyond pilot.

Dev/Hannah — please update nightly_sweep_runbook.md and allocation_proposal_v2.xlsx with the cap and eviction process, then share the updated drive link. Marissa — once done, send the carve-out approval stub to procurement@vertexbio.com and cc legal if any retention amendments are requested.

I approve the temporary carve-out conditioned on the above.

—Marcus
